h: Bouncing Basics and Yorkshire Days Out
p: Nobody wants to spend the first ten minutes of their session queuing at the front desk, so fill in waivers online before you leave home. Bring a water bottle, wear clothes that stretch, and stash phones and keys safely. If you've been before and kept your grip socks, bring them along, as they can usually be reused.

Parents of very young children might want to look at quieter session times, while groups of teens will probably love the livelier weekend slots. Whatever time you pick, the trampoline rules are simple: one jumper per bed, no rough play and follow the staff's instructions.

Leeds has some brilliant days out for families once everyone's had their fill of bouncing. Tropical World in Roundhay Park is home to butterflies, meerkats, reptiles and exotic plants under glass, and it's great for younger kids. Temple Newsam is a grand Tudor-Jacobean house with a working rare-breeds farm on its estate, which makes for a lovely day out in the fresh air.

History fans might enjoy the Thackray Museum of Medicine, which brings the story of health and medicine to life in an interactive and sometimes gloriously gruesome way. A little further out, Harewood House has gardens, a bird garden and grand rooms to explore, and the Leeds Corn Exchange is a beautiful Victorian building full of independent shops.
